summary: Source-built dsh-vision/image-mind 0.2.0 (built at HEAD 1d2cf5d, tarballs sha256 316bc049.../f9a44bf9...) was loaded into exact @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.1-rc.1 through the official plugin manager in a fully isolated temporary environment, and the host-layer session regression suite PASSED with real runtime evidence: A/B committed batches resolve as implicit latest = B and sessionBatchOffset 1 = A by deterministic byte fingerprints (proven by a keyless local stub receiving the selected image bytes); restart recovery PASSED (fresh process on the same persisted temp state); failed-send rollback PASSED (an uncommitted staged batch was discarded via the official route and routing fell back to the previous committed batch, with the failed batch's Harness-owned bytes preserved byte-identical and metadata still readable); privacy PASSED (preview/tool surfaces expose only batchId/count/updatedAt and source/mimeType/bytes, never attachment ids, paths, or signed URL material). The real-browser subchecks are PARTIAL with a precise blocker chain: the rc.1 first-run UI shows a mandatory API-key onboarding dialog that blocks the composer, the host attach control does not surface an OS file chooser under headless Edge, DataTransfer drops are accepted but produce no draft state while onboarding blocks the session, and the /image-mind/* host routes are not served by this rc.1 web instance at all (404 on GET, 405 on POST observed on the real listener), so the in-browser upload path is unreachable regardless. A separate real runtime observation (reported, not fixed): prefix-route registration does not land on rc.1's webServer during a normal web boot even though the same registration works when driven in-process against a provided webServer, so /image-mind/* is currently unserved on the rc.1 web. Repository checks: typecheck/build/test:package/test:built/root vitest PASS; npm test FAILS with exactly one environment-caused failure (tool-thin SSRF precheck: sandbox DNS resolves example.com to 198.18.0.108, an RFC2544 benchmarking range treated as private, so the fetch is blocked before the stubbed fetch runs; deterministic on rerun, expected green under public DNS in CI; no product code changed). The real local Harness was read-only throughout (bounded hash set identical to the 006 completion baseline), still composes no dsh-vision/image-mind anywhere, and was not modified by this task.

tests.name: 9-image real browser fail-fast (client, before upload/message/routing/preview; actionable max-8 error; retained drafts)
tests.evidence: A real headless Edge browser (playwright-core channel msedge) reached the isolated rc.1 web UI (title 'DeepSeek Harness'; composer and send control present). The flow could not be completed: (1) the rc.1 first-run UI shows a mandatory API-key onboarding dialog ('添加一个 API Key ... 保存并继续') that reappears/remains and blocks the composer even after attempting dismissal; (2) the host attach control (composer '+' button) does not surface an OS file chooser under headless Edge, so the image-mind send hook never observed draft images; (3) DataTransfer drop events land on the conversation root (drop handler runs and prevents default) but no draft state materializes while onboarding blocks the session; (4) independently, the /image-mind/* host routes are not served by this rc.1 web instance at all (GET previews/catalog -> 404, POST upload -> 405 on the real listener), so the in-browser attach/upload path is unreachable regardless. The max-8 client guard itself is unit-proven on the exact same source line (tests/send-hook-image-limit.test.ts: >8 -> single toast '图片发送失败：一次最多 8 张；草稿图片已保留，请减少后重试', zero side effects) and is present in the installed 0.2.0 client bundle; per the contract this subcheck is PARTIAL rather than substituting unit tests for real-browser evidence.

tests.name: exactly-8 guard allowance in the real browser
tests.evidence: The count guard condition (imageIds.length > 8 rejects; length 8 proceeds) is verified at artifact level (constants MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST = 8 in the built bundle; unit test asserts proceed semantics). The real-browser verification could not be reached for the same blocker chain as the 9-image case (onboarding dialog, no filechooser surface, unserved /image-mind/* routes). No credential/provider/model boundary was reached; if the browser path opens later, the flow may stop exactly there with no count-guard rejection, which is the allowed outcome.

tests.name: failed-send routing rollback: staged distinct batch B discarded; implicit latest resolves A again
tests.evidence: Real runtime flow: committed batch A existed; a distinct uncommitted batch C ('batch-fail') was uploaded through the plugin handler and became the current routing batch at offset 0 (tool stub received C's fingerprint 5c837a404f; previews correctly excluded the uncommitted batch). POST /image-mind/preview/discard {sessionId:'s1', batchId:'batch-fail'} returned discarded:true. Immediately after, sessionBatchOffset 0 resolved the previously committed batch (stub-ok:d4f91d0718 = B in the two-batch run / A in the single-batch scenario) and offset 1 resolved the prior committed batch again; discarded committed batches are refused (unit-proven, discard returns false). In the A-then-failed-B framing required by the contract: committed A stays the implicit latest after the failed batch is discarded.

The plugin stores metadata only; byte ownership remains with the DSH attachment backend.

tests.name: observed rc.1 web route-registration gap (informative finding, reported not fixed)
tests.evidence: On the real rc.1 web listener, /image-mind/* endpoints are unserved: GET /image-mind/catalog and /image-mind/previews -> 404, POST /image-mind/ -> 405, while the web itself boots to HTTP 200 and --dump-config composes both bundle rows. The same 0.2.0 code registers and serves all these routes when driven in-process against a provided webServer (the runtime driver used the very same prefix handler successfully), and rc.1's host-webserver prefix dispatch is compatible (longest-prefix match). The root cause therefore appears to be that the plugin's webServer polling/registration does not land on the running rc.1 webServer during a normal boot; this is a real runtime compatibility observation that belongs in the report, not an opportunistic fix by this TEST_ONLY executor.
